title: CAMEL: Separate time and timezone, check for truncation
description:
ENC_BCD_DIGITS_0_9 truncates the returned string if a
nibble with 0xf is found, so check for that and don't
read past the end of the string. Go ahead and check for
other non-digits as well.

The timezone is not exactly BCD encoded, unlike the time
digits, so handle it separately.

GSM SMS uses the same encoding, so possibly there should be
a special time encoding to handle this and turn it into a
FT_ABSOLUTE_TIME.

Fix #19298

notes.body: So `tz` can be negative (as offsets from GMT/UTC are given as both positive and negative); would a negative value show up as "GMT +-3 hours" or something such as that?  If so, that seems odd - is that the way negative offsets from GMT/UTC are usually shown?

The `+` in `%+d` is a format flag to printf that shows + for positive integers and - for negative integers, not a literal plus sign here.

https://en.cppreference.com/w/c/io/fprintf

> +: the sign of signed conversions is always prepended to the result of the conversion (by default the result is preceded by minus only when it is negative)
